notes: copilot mid-turn follow-up. Copilot has TWO mid-turn input paths (app.js, CLI 1.0.77): the composer's onSubmit Zf sends with mode = ne?.queued ? "enqueue" : "immediate", and ne.queued is set ONLY by the key predicate hcn (ctrl+q / ctrl+return). So plain Enter mid-turn is STEERING (mode:"immediate") and Ctrl+Q is the true queue. This recipe drives the plain-Enter steering path — copilot's default, and the one matching the scenario's process step 'the transcript shows no turn boundary'. Neither path writes anything at typing time: send() with mode:"immediate" stashes via addImmediateMessagesIfProcessing and returns before any emit. The steered message is materialised by runImmediatePromptPreRequest at an in-turn model-request boundary, which calls recordImmediatePromptEvent → sessionRecordEventJson — so it lands in events.jsonl as a real user.message MID-TURN with no assistant.turn_end before it, and the turn then closes with a single turn_end. The daemon reads that user.message as EventType user_message (activity → working) on a session already working, so it is a no-op, not a flicker: ready is reachable from this transcript ONLY via assistant.turn_end → turn_done. NO queuedTurnSplitter seam is needed — the copilot parser does not implement SplitsQueuedFollowUpTurns, and does not need to: with steering there is only ONE turn, so tailer's updateMidPassTurnBoundary (which arms on turn_done followed by more activity in the same pass) never fires. Even if copilot instead consumed the follow-up as its own turn, this spec still passes: like pi's sibling cell it asserts the scenario's negative invariants (working holds, no ready flicker, no waiting) plus a final ready, NOT two distinct arcs — a collapsed span satisfies all of them. mistral-vibe's cell needed the #988 fix only because its spec explicitly models turn1_settle → queued_turn_start → queued_turn_end. PRESESSION SHAPE (provisional, from code, inherited from the basic-turn sibling): copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch holding only workspace.yaml and writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so processlifecycle.Scanner mints a proc-<PID> row before the fswatcher sees any transcript and the real session arrives under a DIFFERENT id; birth is two phases and every later phase anchors to the REAL session. OBSERVATIONS: tokens and cost are live from assistant.message.outputTokens through the shared capacity price map; model is NOT pinned because --model accepts only "auto" on this account and session.auto_mode_resolved picks between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5 per turn.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears on the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
The first user prompt (a shell sleep 10, so the turn stays working long enough to type into) drives ready → working on the real session

A plain-text follow-up is typed into the TUI mid-turn and steered into the running turn. State must stay working through its arrival — no flicker to ready when the mid-turn user.message lands (spec bullets 1 and 2), and no flicker to waiting (--allow-all means no permission.requested is ever written)

The cycle eventually ends at ready (spec bullet 3) — assistant.turn_end settles the turn once the follow-up has been consumed, whether it was folded into this turn (the steering shape) or run as a subsequent one
